title: The Solitary Creek Origin

features.name: spring source sprite
features.desc-on-touch: A tiny figure of the water itself, still learning that it is separate from stone. The creature-shape of origin, before it became tributary, before it knew to flow.

features.name: flow-memory tower
features.desc-on-touch: Stacked blocks of sediment where the creek has carved its own story, decade by decade. Each layer is a conversation the water had with stone before it learned to speak to other waters.

features.name: gathering plaque
features.desc-on-touch: A stone directory listing where tributaries file themselves: upstream names, origin depths, the catalogue of loneliness before meeting. Each marked as: not yet converged.

features.name: crystal clarity pool
features.desc-on-touch: A pool so clear it becomes a mirror to the sky—the creek still shows heaven's reflection before joining the river. After this, the sky will be less visible from the water.

features.name: solitude arch
features.desc-on-touch: A doorway carved by patient water into patient stone. The shape says: this creek knows how to be alone. This is not loneliness—this is a form of knowledge.

inscription: the creek remembers before it ever learns to forget

file.name: Creek_Origin_Field_Recording_Dawn_Unnamed_Tributary.mp3
file.note: The first moment of flow, captured at sunrise: stone, and the sound of water learning its own voice in absolute silence.

reverie.title: REVERIE — at the creek's birth, before sunrise reaches
narr: You wade into the cold pool where the creek begins.
She stands on the stone bank, recording. The water here
tastes of only itself—no river-taste yet, no mixing.
"Do you feel that?" she says. The water is so clear
it's almost invisible. You are wading in clarity itself.
"It doesn't know it's a tributary yet," she whispers.

exits.label: downward toward the gathering where creeks learn to meet
deeper into the paddock where rain first falls
upstream into the hills where stone remembers being higher
through the grass toward where other waters flow
